Chapter 1: Introduction to Graphs

A graph G = (V, E) consists of a vertex set V and an edge set E. This fixture mirrors the GNN textbook HTML chapter shape for offline ingest.

1.1 Definitions

An undirected graph has symmetric adjacency. A directed graph has ordered pairs. Node features and edge features enable message passing in graph neural networks.

1.2 Examples

Social networks, molecules, citation graphs, and knowledge graphs are common domains. Citation graphs connect papers through bibliography edges.

1.3 Exercises

Exercise: construct the adjacency matrix for a 4-node cycle graph and compute degree. Exercise: distinguish homophily from heterophily on a toy labeled graph.
